attributes.name: POV
attributes.description: Whose viewpoint is the scene told from? (e.g. 1st person, 2nd person, 3rd person)

attributes.name: Time Period
attributes.description: When does the scene take place? (e.g. present, past, future)

attributes.name: Hook
attributes.description: What will convince the reader to start and keep reading this scene?

attributes.name: Purpose
attributes.description: Why is this scene important to the story? Does it advance the plot or develop characters?

attributes.name: Conflict
attributes.description: What two forces or characters are on opposing sides in this scene?

attributes.name: Climax
attributes.description: How does the scene end, and how does it hook the reader into the next scene?

attributes.name: Character Goals
attributes.description: What does your character want or need to achieve in this scene?

attributes.name: Character Development
attributes.description: How does the character change or develop in this scene?

attributes.name: Sensory Detail
attributes.description: How do the five senses (taste, touch, sight, hearing, smell) impact this scene?

sc4.name: Goal, Motivation, Conflict
sc4.description: A foundational approach to writing good scenes

attributes.name: Goal
attributes.description: What does the character want or need to achieve in this scene?

attributes.name: Motivation
attributes.description: What drives the character to pursue their goal in this scene?

attributes.name: Conflict
attributes.description: What stops (or could stop) the character from achieving their goal in this scene?

sc7.name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
sc7.description: Identify how your character's needs are met in this scene using psychologist Abraham Maslow's personality framework

attributes.name: Physiological Needs
attributes.description: Level 1: How are the character's biological needs for survival being met in this scene? (e.g. food, shelter, clothing, sex)

attributes.name: Safety Needs
attributes.description: Level 2: How is the character's need for safety and security being met in this scene? (e.g. financially, emotionally, socially)

attributes.name: Love and Belongingness Needs
attributes.description: Level 3: How is the character's need for belonging being met in this scene? (e.g. friendship, trust, acceptance, love)

attributes.name: Esteem Needs
attributes.description: Level 4: How is the character's need for self-esteem and respect from others being met in this scene? (e.g. status, prestige)

attributes.name: Self-Actualization Needs
attributes.description: Level 5: How is the character's need for self-fulfillment being met in this scene? (e.g. achieving one's full potential)

sc11.name: Plot Problem Evaluation
sc11.description: Part of the Story Genius Method, this scene template is designed to help you evaluate whether or not a plot idea you have is right for your story.

attributes.name: Is the problem capable of forcing my character to make the inner change that my novel is actually about?
Will the problem force my character to struggle with their misbelief?
Will the approaching consequence cost my character something big emotionally speaking even if he/she doesn't achieve their goal?

sc1.name: Proactive Scene
sc1.description: Inspired by Scene & Sequel and the Snowflake Method

attributes.name: Goal
attributes.description: What does the character want or need to achieve in this scene?

attributes.name: Conflict
attributes.description: What stops (or could stop) the character from achieving their goal in this scene?

attributes.name: Setback
attributes.description: What takes away the agency or power of the character in this scene?

sc2.name: Reactive Scene
sc2.description: Inspired by Scene & Sequel and the Snowflake Method

attributes.name: Reaction
attributes.description: How does the character respond to the setback in the previous scene?

attributes.name: Dilemma
attributes.description: What choices does the character have to respond to their setback? Where will each choice lead?

attributes.name: Decision
attributes.description: What does the character decide to do in response to their setback?

sc8.name: Sarra Cannon's Scene Roadmap
sc8.description: Create a roadmap for your scene with this template by author and self-publishing expert Sarra Cannon

attributes.name: Who is the point-of-view character in this scene?
What is my character's desire or goal in this scene?
Why is this desire or goal important to my character?
What will happen if they fail? What's at stake?
What obstacle or conflict will they face in this scene?
What will we learn about my character in this scene?
How will this scene change them or their path forward?
How does this scene fit into my character's overall arc?
How does this scene fit into the overall story arc or plot?

sc10.name: Story Genius
sc10.description: Part of the Story Genius Method, this scene template helps you craft scenes that are meaningful to both your plot and your characters by knowing the alpha point, sub plot, plod, third rail, and what happens next in the story.

attributes.name: The Alpha Point
attributes.description: The key role the scene will play in your novel's cause-and-effect trajectory. The alpha point must tell you why this scene is necessary and relevant to the story.

attributes.name: Subplot
attributes.description: Fill this when you name the subplots you encounter based on which character's subplot it is. Ex: Lucy's subplot. If you have a plotline for that subplot, move this scene card there.

attributes.name: Plot
attributes.description: What happens in the first part of the scene? (Cause) What is the external consequence of what happens in the scene? (Effect)

attributes.name: The Third Rail (desire + misbelief)
attributes.description: Why does what is happening matter to your protagonist? What realization does this event trigger within the protagonist to impact their desire and misbelief? This realization must lead to action.

attributes.name: And so?
attributes.description: What must happen next as a result of what occurred in this scene? Needs to be a concrete action-based event like the alpha point.

sc9.name: Susanne Lakin Scene
sc9.description: Craft your perfect scene with this template by author and writing coach Susanne (C.S.) Lakin

attributes.name: How much time passed since previous scene with this character
What main way is the story advanced? What new plot points are revealed?
What conflicts/obstacles are presented in the scene?
How does the POV character change or grow by the end of the scene?
The high moment or key info revealed in scene
Important backstory bits revealed in scene
World-building or specific setting/locale details brought out

sc6.name: Three Story Scene
sc6.description: Based on the book Three Story Method by J. Thorn

attributes.name: Conflict
attributes.description: What is the central conflict of the scene?

attributes.name: Choice
attributes.description: What choice do the characters make to deal with the scene's conflict?

attributes.name: Consequence
attributes.description: What is the consequence of the choice? Use the consequence as a hook to the next scene

sc5.name: W Scene
sc5.description: Based on the W Plot method

attributes.name: Trigger Event
attributes.description: The scene's opening event, which places the protagonist into difficult circumstances

attributes.name: 1st Turning Point
attributes.description: An event or choice that briefly improves the protagonist's circumstances

attributes.name: 2nd Trigger Event
attributes.description: An event at the "scene midpoint" that presents the protagonist with further difficulty

attributes.name: 2nd Turning Point
attributes.description: At the scene's darkest moment, circumstances improve again, leading to the scene's climax

attributes.name: Resolution
attributes.description: Wrap up the scene's central conflict and hook the reader into the next scene or chapter
